title: Money and Shopping
description: Ten short stories, diary entries and letters about money: saving for a toy, a family budget, a first paycheck, a small food business, a used car, a visit to the bank, a wedding on a budget, a new apartment, a yard sale and a grandfather's advice.

lessons.title: Leo Saves for a Dragon
lessons.summary: A nine-year-old boy saves his own money for a toy dragon.
lessons.text:
Leo was nine years old. Every day, he walked home from school past a small toy store. One afternoon, he saw something new in the store's display window. It was a big green dragon with gold wings. Its wings could open and close, and its eyes were red.

Leo stopped and looked at the dragon for a long time. A small card in the display said "$45." That was a lot of money for a boy who was only nine.

At dinner, Leo told his mother about the dragon. "Can you buy it for me?" he asked. His mother refused. "I'm sorry, but I'm not going to buy it," she said. "It isn't cheap. But you can save your own money for it. If you save a little every week, you will have enough eventually."

Leo wasn't happy at first, but he thought about it all night. He had $9 in a box under his bed, so he needed $36 more. The next morning, his mother said that she would pay him $3 a week if he helped at home. He had to clean his room, help in the garden and wash the car with his father.

Leo made a plan. His aim was simple: $45 for the dragon. He wrote his aim on a piece of paper and put it on the wall above his bed. Every week, he put $3 in the box.

Some weeks were hard. Once, his friends bought ice cream after school, and Leo wanted some too. But he refused. "I'm saving for my dragon," he told them.

Every day, Leo walked past the store and looked at the display. The dragon was still there. "I hope nobody buys it before I do," he thought.

Eventually, after 9 weeks, Leo counted his money. He had $45! He ran to the store with his mother. The woman in the store took the dragon out of the display and gave it to him.

"You worked hard for this," his mother said. "You deserve it." Leo felt proud. "It wasn't cheap," he said, "but I paid for it myself."

Questions:
How old was Leo?
Leo was nine years old.
Where did Leo see the dragon?
He saw it in the display window of a small toy store.
Why did his mother refuse to buy the dragon?
She refused because it wasn't cheap, and she wanted Leo to save his own money.
What was Leo's aim?
His aim was to save $45 for the dragon.
Did Leo have enough money eventually?
Yes. Eventually, after 9 weeks, he had $45.
Why did Leo deserve the dragon?
He deserved it because he worked hard and paid for it himself.

lessons.title: Our First Budget
lessons.summary: A young couple makes a budget, stops buying coffee at a shop and saves money.
lessons.text:
Last year, my husband Dan and I had a problem with money. We both had jobs, but at the end of every month, our bank account was almost empty. We didn't know where the money went. This caused a lot of stress.

One evening, Dan sat down at the table with a pen and some paper. "We need a budget," he said. "Otherwise, we will never save any money." I agreed with him.

That evening, we wrote down everything we paid for in one month. First, there were the big payments: the payment for our home, the car payment and the payment for our phones. Then there were the small things. When we added them up, we were surprised. I bought a coffee every morning on my way to work. Each coffee cost $5. That was more than $100 a month just for coffee!

The next day, we made a budget for the next month. We decided how much we could spend on food, clothes and fun. We also looked for things to remove from our lives. It was easy to remove 2 TV services that we never watched.

Then we made a rule: no coffee from the coffee shop. We banned it for 3 months. At first, the ban was hard for me. But I bought a good coffee machine and made coffee at home. To be honest, my coffee at home was just as good. A cup of coffee at home cost only 50 cents. Therefore, the ban was a very good idea.

Every Sunday evening, we sat down together and looked at the budget. Was it effective? Yes, it was very effective. After 3 months, there was $900 in our savings account. Therefore, we decided to keep the ban, but only on work days. On weekends, we sometimes go to the coffee shop together, and now it feels special.

The budget didn't only help our bank account. It also helped us. There is much less stress in our home now. If you have the same problem, you should try a budget too. It might feel hard at first, but it is very effective.

Questions:
Why did the woman and her husband feel stress?
They felt stress because their bank account was almost empty at the end of every month.
What did Dan say one evening?
He said that they needed a budget, otherwise they would never save any money.
How much did the woman spend on coffee every month?
She spent more than $100 a month on coffee.
What was easy to remove?
It was easy to remove 2 TV services that they never watched.
Was the budget effective?
Yes, it was very effective. They saved $900 in 3 months.

lessons.title: My First Paycheck
lessons.summary: A sixteen-year-old writes in her diary about her first summer job at a food store.
lessons.text:
Saturday, June 1

Today was my first day at work! I'm 16, and I have a summer job at Hill's Market, a small food store on our street. My job is at the cash register. Mr. Hill, the owner, showed me how to use the register. You put each thing near the register, and the price appears on the screen.

Mr. Hill said that the person at the register is responsible for the money. "At the end of the day, the money in the register has to be right," he said. I want to be responsible, so I counted the money twice.

Friday, June 14

Today I got my first paycheck! I worked 40 hours in 2 weeks, and I get $12 an hour. So I thought the check would be $480. But it was only $430. At first, I didn't fully understand why. Mr. Hill explained that some of the money goes to taxes. "Everybody pays taxes," he said. "Taxes pay for roads, schools and other things that benefit everybody." Now I fully understand. $430 is the most money I have ever had!

Wednesday, June 19

I have noticed a pattern at the store. Every day at 5, a lot of people come in after work, and the line at the register gets very long. The same pattern happens every Saturday morning. Today I told Mr. Hill about the pattern. I said that we should have 2 people at the register at those times. He tried it this afternoon, and it worked. He said that he appreciated my idea. "I highly appreciate workers who think," he told me.

Friday, June 28

My second paycheck came today. I put half of it in the bank. Mom says that saving is a good habit, and it will benefit me all my life. With the other half, I bought dinner for my family. Everybody was surprised. Dad said that he really appreciated it. Mr. Hill also said that he thinks very highly of me, and he wants me to work at the store next summer too. I'm going to say yes!

Questions:
Where does the girl work?
She works at the cash register at Hill's Market.
What is the person at the register responsible for?
The person at the register is responsible for the money.
Why was her first paycheck smaller than she thought?
It was smaller because some of the money went to taxes.
What pattern did she notice at the store?
She noticed that a lot of people come in every day at 5, after work.
What did Mr. Hill say about her idea?
He said that he appreciated her idea.

lessons.title: Ana's Food Business
lessons.summary: A woman leaves a large company and starts a small business that brings home-cooked food to offices.
lessons.text:
Ana worked at a large corporation for 10 years. She had a good job, but she wasn't happy. In her free time, she loved to cook. Her food had a wonderful taste, and her friends always asked for more.

One day, Ana had an idea for a small business. The concept was simple: fresh, home-cooked food, brought to offices in the city every day at 12. The concept appealed to her friend Rosa right away. "The food near my office is terrible," Rosa said. "I would pay for that every day."

Ana left the corporation and started her business at home. But she had a problem. Nobody knew about her food. She needed a strategy to promote it. How do you promote food when nobody has tasted it?

Her first strategy was an ad in the local paper. The ad was small, and it cost $200, but only 3 people called her. The ad didn't work well.

Then Rosa gave her some advice. "You should make a profile online," she said. "Put photos of your food on your profile. People will see the photos and share them." Ana made a profile and posted a new photo every day.

Her second strategy was even better. She gave away free food in front of a large office building. "If people taste it, they will buy it," she said. She was right. A man put a piece of chicken in his mouth and closed his eyes. "This is the best food I have tasted all year," he said. A woman next to him tried some too. Her mouth was still full when she asked, "How much does it cost?" That same day, 20 people ordered food.

Ana also had a big advantage over the large food corporations: her food was fresh. Food from a big corporation might sit in a store for days. Ana's food was always cooked the same morning. She used this advantage in her next ad: "Cooked this morning. On your desk by 12."

After 6 months, Ana had 80 customers. She worked harder than before, but the work really appealed to her.

Questions:
Where did Ana work for 10 years?
She worked at a large corporation.
What was the concept of her business?
The concept was fresh, home-cooked food, brought to offices in the city every day at 12.
Why didn't her first ad work well?
It didn't work well because only 3 people called her.
What did Rosa say Ana should do?
She said that Ana should make a profile online and put photos of her food on it.
What advantage did Ana have over the large corporations?
Her food was always fresh, because it was cooked the same morning.

lessons.title: Ben Buys a Used Car
lessons.summary: A young man and his father check a used car, get a quote for repairs and agree on a fair price.
lessons.text:
Ben was 18, and he just got his driver's license. Now he needed a car. He had $5,000 from his summer jobs. A new car cost too much, so he decided to buy a used one.

He looked online and found a small blue car for $4,500. It was sold by an older woman named Mrs. Lee, who lived on the coast. On Saturday, Ben and his father drove 2 hours to the coast to see the car.

The car looked good. Mrs. Lee said that she only drove short distances, to the store and back. She never drove long distances, so the car had only 40,000 miles on it. Ben's father was happy about that, but he wanted to look closer. "We should look under the car," he told Ben. "Cars on the coast sometimes have problems, because the sea air is bad for metal."

He looked at the bottom of the car. The metal at the bottom was fine. But at the edge of one door, he found a small brown spot. "The metal at this edge is getting old," he said. "It isn't a big problem now, but it might be a problem later."

Then Ben tried the doors. One door didn't lock. He pressed the button on the key again and again, but the door didn't lock. Also, when Ben drove the car, he heard a strange sound from the engine. "That's strange," said his father. "We have to find out what that sound is before we buy the car."

They took the car to a repair shop in the town. The man at the shop listened to the strange sound and looked at the door lock. Then he gave them a quote: $600 to fix everything.

Ben showed the quote to Mrs. Lee. "I don't think the price is correct for this car," he said. "Is $3,900 fair?" Mrs. Lee looked at the quote for a minute. "You're correct," she said. "The car needs some work. $3,900 is fair."

Ben paid $3,900, and the car was fixed the next week. Now every door locks, and the engine is quiet. Ben is very happy with his first car.

Questions:
What did Ben just get?
He just got his driver's license.
Where did Mrs. Lee live?
She lived on the coast.
Why did Ben's father want to look under the car?
Because the sea air on the coast is bad for metal.
What did he find at the edge of one door?
He found a small brown spot.
What was the quote from the repair shop?
The quote was $600 to fix everything.
How much did Ben pay for the car?
He paid $3,900.

lessons.title: A Visit to the Bank
lessons.summary: An older woman finds a payment she didn't make, and the bank helps her get her money back.
lessons.text:
Rose was 78 years old. She was a senior citizen who used the same bank all her life. Rose had 2 accounts at the bank: her primary account, where her money from the government came every month, and a savings account.

One morning, Rose looked at her primary account on her phone. She saw a strange payment of $800 to a store in another city. Rose didn't make that payment. She wanted to call the bank, but her phone had a bad connection, and she couldn't hear anything. So she went to the bank.

At the bank, a young man named Sam helped her. He looked at her account and said that she was probably the victim of a crime. "I'm sorry, but you are a victim," he said. "Someone has stolen your card number. Many older citizens are victims of this crime every year."

Sam locked her card right away. Then he told her that the bank would open an investigation. "The investigation might take 2 weeks," he said.

Rose was worried. "Will I get my money back?" she asked. Sam explained that every account at the bank has protection. "All our customers have protection against payments that they didn't make. If the investigation shows that you didn't make the payment, the money will be returned to you."

Then Sam gave her a number to call. "You can call this number to check the status of the investigation," he said. "You can also check the status online. A green light on the page will indicate that the investigation is closed."

After 10 days, Rose got a call from the bank. The status of the investigation was "closed." The $800 was returned to her primary account. Sam also told her some good news: the police caught the man who stole the card numbers. He was caught in another state.

Rose thanked Sam. "If I see a strange payment again, I will come to the bank right away," she said.

Questions:
How many accounts did Rose have at the bank?
She had 2 accounts: her primary account and a savings account.
What did Rose see on her phone?
She saw a strange payment of $800 to a store in another city.
Why didn't Rose call the bank?
Because her phone had a bad connection, and she couldn't hear anything.
What did Sam say about the money?
He said that the money would be returned to her if the investigation showed that she didn't make the payment.
How can Rose check the status of the investigation?
She can call a number or check the status online. A green light on the page will indicate that the investigation is closed.

lessons.title: A Wedding on a Budget
lessons.summary: A couple plans a small, happy wedding without spending a lot of money.
lessons.text:
Tom and Sara were going to get married in the summer. The year before, Sara's cousin had a very big wedding. It was like a royal wedding, with 300 people, a band and a very large dinner. But Tom and Sara had a small budget: only $5,000.

"We don't need a royal wedding," Sara said. "We just need a happy one." Tom was glad that she felt that way. He felt the same.

First, they needed a place for the wedding. They found a small hotel next to a river. The hotel had a garden for 60 people. "You have to reserve the garden early," the woman at the hotel told them. "People reserve it 6 months before the wedding." So Tom and Sara reserved it the same day.

Next, Sara needed a dress. She looked at some fashion magazines, but the dresses in them cost thousands of dollars. Then her mother showed her an old box. Inside was her mother's own wedding dress. "Fashion changes, but this dress is still beautiful," her mother said. Sara tried it on, and it was perfect.

Tom needed a suit. He didn't want to spend much on a suit that he would only wear a few times. He found a dark blue suit for $90 at a second-hand store. "It looks like a $1,000 suit," his brother said. Tom was glad.

On the day of the wedding, the sun was shining. Their friends brought food, and a friend who played the guitar played music for them as a gift.

After dinner, Tom's brother gave a speech. In his speech, he said that Tom was a good brother and that Sara was the best thing in Tom's life. Then Sara's father gave a short speech. He said that he was glad to welcome Tom into the family. Everybody cried a little during the speeches.

At the end of the evening, Tom and Sara left in an old car. Everybody stood in the street and waved. Tom and Sara waved back until they couldn't see their friends anymore. The wedding cost only $4,800, and it was the happiest day of their lives.

Questions:
Why didn't Tom and Sara want a royal wedding?
Because they had a small budget, and they just wanted a happy wedding.
What did the woman at the hotel say?
She said that they had to reserve the garden early.
Where did Sara's wedding dress come from?
It was her mother's own wedding dress.
How much did Tom's suit cost?
His suit cost $90.
What did Tom's brother say in his speech?
He said that Tom was a good brother and that Sara was the best thing in Tom's life.

lessons.title: Nora's New Home
lessons.summary: In an e-mail to her sister, a woman describes how she found a new apartment near her job.
lessons.text:
Hi Kate,

I have big news! I have finally found a new apartment, and I'm going to move next month. Let me tell you how it happened.

As you know, I started a new job at the airport in March. My old place was 1 hour from the airport, so I needed something closer. I called a real estate agent named Mr. Diaz. He works for a small real estate company in the city.

Mr. Diaz showed me 3 places. The first one was in a big complex right next to the airport. It was cheap, and I could walk to work. But the noise from the planes was terrible. Mr. Diaz said that the noise might affect my sleep. I knew it would affect me, so I said no.

The second place was across the bridge, in an old house. It looked nice, but the walls in one room weren't dry, and Mr. Diaz found a problem with the foundation. "A problem with the foundation is a serious problem," he said. "If the foundation isn't strong, it will affect the whole house." So I said no again.

The third place was in a small complex on the other side of the bridge, 15 minutes from the airport. The complex was built 5 years ago, and it is very clean. Behind the complex, there is a little stream with trees on both sides. When you open the window, you can hear the water of the stream flow over the stones. The rooms are warm in winter and dry all year. The water flows well in the bathroom, too. It costs $1,200 a month, which is fair for this part of the city.

I signed the papers the same day. Mr. Diaz has worked in real estate for 20 years, and he said that it was a very good place for the money.

You should come and visit! In the summer, we can sit next to the stream in the warm evening air. Just tell me when your plane lands, and I'll pick you up at the airport.

Love,
Nora

Questions:
Why did Nora need a new place?
Because her old place was 1 hour from her new job at the airport.
Why didn't Nora take the first place?
Because the noise from the planes might affect her sleep.
What problem did the second place have?
It had a problem with the foundation.
What is behind the third complex?
There is a little stream with trees on both sides.
What are the rooms like?
The rooms are warm in winter and dry all year.
How much does the new apartment cost?
It costs $1,200 a month.

lessons.title: The Yard Sale
lessons.summary: A husband and wife sell their old things in front of their house and make a friendly bet.
lessons.text:
Mike and Linda lived in an old house. After 25 years in the house, they had a lot of old objects. There were boxes of objects in every room. "We should have a yard sale," Linda said one evening. "We don't need all these things, and other people might use them."

Mike agreed. "I bet we can make more than $300," he said with a smile. Linda smiled too. "I bet we can't," she said. "Most of these things are very old." So they made a bet. The person who lost the bet would buy dinner.

First, they checked the weather. The weather report said that Saturday would be warm and sunny. "Perfect weather for a yard sale," Mike said.

On Friday, they carried everything out of the house. There were old tools from Mike's father, sports equipment from when their children were young, a pair of skis, 3 pairs of boots, a lamp and many other objects. They put a price on every object.

On Saturday morning, people started to come at 8. An old man looked at Mike's tools for a long time. "These tools are older than me," he said, "but good tools never die." He bought all the tools for $60. A young mother bought the sports equipment for her kids. A student bought the pair of skis and left with a big smile.

All day, their fat old cat slept on a box in the sun. A little girl wanted to buy the fat cat. "I'm sorry, the cat isn't for sale," Linda said with a smile. The girl smiled and touched the cat's head.

At 4, Mike counted the money. They made $420. "I won the bet!" Mike said. Linda laughed. "You won the bet, so I'll buy dinner," she said.

That evening, they ate at their favorite restaurant. Their house had much more space now, and they had $420 in the bank. "Let's have another yard sale next year," Mike said with a smile.

Questions:
Why did Linda want to have a yard sale?
Because they didn't need all their old things, and other people might use them.
What bet did Mike and Linda make?
Mike said that they could make more than $300, and Linda said that they couldn't.
What did the weather report say?
It said that Saturday would be warm and sunny.
Who bought Mike's old tools?
An old man bought all the tools for $60.
What did the young mother buy?
She bought the sports equipment for her kids.
How much money did they make?
They made $420, so Mike won the bet.

lessons.title: A Letter from Grandpa
lessons.summary: A grandfather writes to his grandson about saving money and tells him what he learned as a young soldier.
lessons.text:
Dear Jake,

I really enjoyed our conversation on the phone last Sunday. We talked about a lot of things: your new job, sports and even politics. But one part of our conversation has stayed with me. You said that saving money is boring and that you want to enjoy your life now. To some extent, you are right. You are young, and you should enjoy your life. But let me tell you a little story.

When I was 20, I was a soldier. The army sent me to a small town near the border with Canada. There wasn't much to do near the border, so the young soldiers spent most of their money on fun. We were paid once a month, and most soldiers had no money left after a few days.

Then an older soldier named Frank gave me some advice. He said, "Save a little from every check. Money in the bank gives you freedom." At that time, I didn't fully understand him. But I started to save $20 every month. After 3 years in the army, I had enough money to go to college.

Later in life, I learned what that freedom truly means. When I got sick at 60, I couldn't work for a whole year. But your grandmother and I saved for many years, so we didn't have to worry about money while I was sick. We also never had any debt, because we thought of debt as the enemy. That was our rule, and debt never became our enemy.

I'm not saying that you should save every dollar. To a large extent, life is for living. But I truly believe that you should save a little every month. If you save 10 percent of every check, you will have freedom when you need it most.

I truly enjoy our conversations. And please don't start a conversation about politics with your grandmother. You know that she has very strong opinions!

Love,
Grandpa

Questions:
What did Grandpa and Jake talk about on the phone?
They talked about Jake's new job, sports and politics.
What did Jake say about saving money?
He said that saving money is boring and that he wants to enjoy his life now.
Where was Grandpa sent as a young soldier?
He was sent to a small town near the border with Canada.
What advice did the older soldier give him?
He said that Grandpa should save a little from every check, because money in the bank gives you freedom.
Why didn't Grandpa have to worry about money when he was sick?
Because he and his wife saved for many years.
